procedure: Give each parallel coding agent its own linked git worktree (separate working directory + index) instead of having all agents share one working directory, so concurrent file writes and git operations never collide.
experiment: Built a real, reproducible local experiment (run_experiment.py): initialized a throwaway git repo, then ran 8 concurrent 'agents' (real OS threads each spawning real git subprocesses) twice -- once all operating in ONE shared working directory (checkout+edit+commit), once each with its own `git worktree add` linked worktree -- and measured how many of the 8 landed a clean commit in each scenario.
notes: Cleanest, most decisive result of this pass: 1/8 -> 8/8 success rate under real concurrent git operations, at a modest (~0.6s for 8 agents) overhead cost. Directly reproduces the claimed mechanism, not a proxy.

artifact: StealthLab's own deferred/searchable-tool mechanism (native -- this session's own tool list is the evidence, not a third-party artifact)
procedure: Advertise only tool NAMES for less-common tools up front; load a tool's full JSON-Schema definition only when ToolSearch is actually called for it, instead of shipping every tool's full schema in every system prompt regardless of whether it is used this conversation.
experiment: Measured, with tiktoken (cl100k_base), the real token cost of this session's own actual deferred tool-name listing (25 tools, names only) vs. the real, freshly-fetched full JSON-Schema definitions (via this session's own ToolSearch call) for 4 of those same tools (WebFetch, WebSearch, CronCreate, PushNotification).
notes: CAVEAT: CronCreate and PushNotification's description text was lightly abbreviated (special characters removed) to write the measurement file reliably -- their real production schemas are LONGER than measured here, so 377.8 tokens/tool and the 67.5x ratio are a conservative LOWER BOUND, not an overstatement. WebFetch and WebSearch were measured verbatim (only em-dashes normalized to hyphens, negligible token effect). This validates seeds 12/13/18's claim using StealthLab's own already-deployed implementation, not a new external adoption.
